objective: Real, exact du-style byte-level sizes of the live main DB, replacement_main.db, cold_segments/ total, and the theoretical post-cutover production footprint.

live_main_db.method: stat -f %z (exact file size in bytes) + du -sh (human-readable cross-check)

cold_segments_total.note: du -sh reported 1.0G total across all 41 segment files; du -ch sum of individual files also reported 1.0G total, consistent.

total_p5a_candidate_footprint.note: cold_segments bytes is the 1.0G du -sh figure converted to bytes (approximate, since du -sh rounds); exact byte-level per-file sum not separately captured but du -ch's own total agreed at 1.0G so this is a tight approximation, not a rough estimate.

theoretical_post_cutover_footprint.method: PRAGMA dbstat (SQLite's built-in page-level size introspection virtual table) was used to measure transfer_index's REAL on-disk footprint including all 5 of its indexes (idx_transfer_destination_time, idx_transfer_source_time, idx_transfer_block_time, idx_transfer_indexed_at, idx_transfer_valid) directly against the live production DB: 2,182,950,912 bytes (~2.18 GB) for 5,284,432 transfer_index rows at time of measurement, i.e. ~413.09 bytes/row (table+indexes combined).
theoretical_post_cutover_footprint.cold_fraction_source: Part 14 frozen accounting: 1,735,652 COLD / 5,223,038 total at high-water id 6648855
theoretical_post_cutover_footprint.important_caveat: This is a PROPORTIONAL ESTIMATE, not a direct measurement of a post-cutover DB (P5A does not delete anything from production, per the explicit hard-stop/forbidden-action list). The estimate applies the measured COLD row fraction (33.2%) to the measured transfer_index table+index bytes (2.18 GB), NOT to the whole 14.95 GB file (transfer_index is only ~14.6% of the total file size -- the rest is the 275 other tables, indexes, and free/overallocated pages). VACUUM would additionally be needed after any real row deletion to physically reclaim freed pages (SQLite does not automatically shrink a file on DELETE without VACUUM or auto_vacuum); this estimate assumes a VACUUM is included in any real future cutover, otherwise the freed pages would remain allocated inside the file (logically empty, physically still occupying 14.95 GB) until a VACUUM runs.
theoretical_post_cutover_footprint.reclaim_is_modest_by_design: The 4.85% reclaim is intentionally modest because HOT is defined generously (90-day recency window UNION broad pinning criteria), which is a deliberate P5A/P4 design choice favoring safety and evidence-completeness over maximum storage reduction -- COLD only captures older, unpinned, historically-inactive rows. The benefit of the split is NOT primarily disk reclaim; it is bounding HOT's steady-state growth (see Part 29) and improving RECENT_ONLY query latency (see Part 26), with disk reclaim being a secondary, smaller benefit.

note: All primary size figures (live main DB, replacement_main.db, cold_segments/) are exact byte-level measurements via stat/du, not estimates. Only the theoretical post-cutover footprint is a disclosed proportional estimate, since P5A never performs an actual cutover or deletion against production.
